title: Microsoft Dataverse: richer record labels for Copilot /mention in Microsoft 365 apps
summary: The roadmap facts, record-label behaviour and environment-level admin path are supported. Hold because the page says the labels' arrival behaviour is not stated but also promises that environments already allowing record search will receive the labels without another step. The action rating and role guidance also need small corrections.

claims.claim: The change gives Dataverse, Dynamics 365 and Power Apps record references in Microsoft 365 Copilot Context IQ richer labels containing environment, app and table information.
claims.quote: End users of Microsoft 365 Copilot will see improved Microsoft Dataverse, Dynamics 365, and Power Apps record references in Context IQ with richer, more descriptive labels that include environment, app, and table information.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls
claims.claim: The setting is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Search > Search for records in Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; controls[0].scope; summary; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Search for records in Microsoft 365 apps controls /mention record availability per environment, and changes are saved in that environment.
claims.quote: On the Environments page, select an environment. ... Under the Search section, turn on Search for records in Microsoft 365 apps. ... Select Save to apply the changes.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No API or automation for this specific /mention setting is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Search for records in Microsoft 365 apps" with API, PowerShell, pac, Power Platform API and organization; opened /mention and Organization entity reference; searched reference for mention, Microsoft 365, Office 365, Context IQ and search. No matching setting mapping found.

claims.where: controls[0].note; summary; Governance controls
claims.claim: No separate switch for the richer label format is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse record labels enable; Dataverse enhanced label default enable; /mention label switch Dataverse. Opened /mention and Manage feature settings; found the general record-search setting, not a separate label-format switch.

claims.where: What's changing; Open questions; summary; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Learn describes enhanced labels as Environment Name + App Name + Record Name, unlike the roadmap's table wording.
claims.quote: Each record is displayed with an enhanced label that includes the Environment Name + App Name + Record Name, helping users quickly identify the correct record and its source.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The records offered through /mention are recently viewed Dynamics 365 and Power Apps records, including model-driven app records.
claims.quote: Most recently viewed Dynamics 365 and Power Apps records are available in Microsoft 365 Copilot through the /mention experience

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: If the same record is opened through multiple apps, its label reflects the most recently used app.
claims.quote: If you access the same record through multiple apps, the label reflects the most recently used app from which you viewed the record.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A viewed record can take up to 15 minutes to become available for /mention.
claims.quote: It can take up to 15 minutes after you view a record on your Dynamics 365 or model-driven apps before you can /mention that record on Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in your productivity apps, like Outlook web client.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The Learn page describes the experience in Outlook on the web, Copilot Chat, Researcher, Word and Teams.
claims.quote: Link to business records in email messages in your Outlook web client ... Link to business records in Copilot Chat, Researcher, Word, and Teams clients

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Manage feature settings lists Search for records in Microsoft 365 apps with a default value of On.
claims.quote: | Search for records in Microsoft 365 apps | You can quickly enable your users to access the records they most recently used in their application. The records are available in the Outlook Web client using a simple /mention gesture. | On |

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated arrival behaviour specifically for the new label format, so its defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse Copilot mention enhanced labels licensing default enable; Dataverse enhanced label default enable. Read roadmap, /mention and Manage feature settings: label contents and the general setting's On default are stated, but no label-specific rollout/default instruction was found.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A small set of Dataverse data syncs with Microsoft 365 for this experience.
claims.quote: A small set of data from Dataverse syncs with Microsoft 365 data.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The sync can cross geographic boundaries in multi-geo organisations.
claims.quote: This sync might cross geo boundaries for multi-geo organizations where the Dataverse data might be in a different geographic region than the data stored for a user in Microsoft 365.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The sync crosses service and compliance boundaries between Dataverse and Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Be aware that this sync also crosses service and compliance boundaries between the two platforms.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Synced data includes environment name, app name, record name and a link to the most recently used record.
claims.quote: Synced data includes the environment name, app name, and record name, and a link to the most recently used record.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Researcher uses a referenced record as contextual grounding.
claims.quote: Currently, Researcher uses the referenced record as contextual grounding to gather and synthesize information from the web and your Microsoft 365 productivity data (such as emails, files, meetings, and chats).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Researcher does not currently retrieve or reason over live Dynamics 365 or Power Apps data associated with the referenced record.
claims.quote: Researcher doesn't currently retrieve or reason over live Dynamics 365 or Power Apps data associated with the referenced record.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Only records a user has access to and has most recently used are offered.
claims.quote: Security is top of mind, so only records that a user has access to and most recently used are available in the Microsoft 365 Copilot and productivity apps.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: An email recipient needs environment access, security roles granting data access and access to the shared record.
claims.quote: The recipient of the email must have access to the environment with security roles that grant access to the data and must be able to access the shared record.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: No further /mention-specific authorisation mechanism is described.
claims.quote: Searched: /mention Dataverse authorization. Opened /mention; it states existing user access and recipient security-role requirements, without describing the internal authorisation mechanism for this record-reference sync.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Updates to synced data update the record in Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: If you make any changes to the synced data, including updates or deletions, the record updates or deletes in Microsoft 365.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Deletions of synced data delete the record in Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: If you make any changes to the synced data, including updates or deletions, the record updates or deletes in Microsoft 365.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Copilot uses a referenced record as context to ground its response.
claims.quote: Copilot uses the referenced record as context to ground its response and perform actions against the relevant business data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The page says Copilot can perform actions against the relevant business data.
claims.quote: Copilot uses the referenced record as context to ground its response and perform actions against the relevant business data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The page does not enumerate the actions against business data enabled by referencing a record.
claims.quote: Searched: /mention Dataverse actions. Opened /mention: it asserts actions against relevant business data and gives productivity examples, but no enumerated catalogue of business-data operations enabled by a record reference.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing specifically for this label change is not published, so the licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: /mention licensing Copilot Dataverse; Dataverse Copilot mention enhanced labels licensing default enable; site:learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin mention license. Opened /mention and Power Platform licensing overview; no licence rule specifically for the label change found.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The /mention Learn page and roadmap name no licence or meter for this change.
claims.quote: Searched: /mention licensing Copilot Dataverse. Read the supplied roadmap and /mention page in full: the latter documents the environment setting and usage, without a licence prerequisite or billing meter.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No charge for this setting or separate meter for the label change is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Search for records in Microsoft 365 apps default labels pricing meter; /mention licensing Copilot Dataverse. Opened /mention, Manage feature settings and Power Platform licensing overview; no setting charge or label-specific meter found.

claims.where: Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The /mention page leaves the admin role unstated, but the cited general feature-settings page requires System Administrator or equivalent permissions.
claims.quote: Make sure you have the System Administrator security role or equivalent permissions to update the settings.
claims.fix: Replace both role-gap sentences with: 'The /mention page does not name a role; Manage feature settings requires the System Administrator security role or equivalent permissions to update these settings.' The supporting page is already cited: https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/settings-features.

claims.where: Why it matters; front matter: defaultState
claims.claim: Existing enabled environments will receive the new labels without an administrator taking another step, although the page records arrival behaviour as unknown.
claims.quote: Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival for the new labels ... Service owners who already allowed the setting will see the new labels without taking any step that Microsoft has documented.
claims.fix: Remove 'Service owners who already allowed the setting will see the new labels without taking any step that Microsoft has documented.' Keep defaultState unknown and the existing statement that Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival; the sources checked do not give a label-specific rollout instruction.

claims.where: front matter: action; Why it matters
claims.claim: The cosmetic replacement of labels used by existing /mention users is a review item.
claims.quote: action: "review" ... The practical view is that this is a review item, not an emergency. ... Records ... get a more descriptive label.
claims.fix: Set action to 'prepare' and replace 'The practical view is that this is a review item, not an emergency.' with 'The practical view is that this needs communication, not emergency action.' The assessment scale assigns prepare to low-risk redesigns of existing experiences that need communication, including when defaultState is unknown.
